name: Ephedrine / ECA stack
lead: The ECA stack combines ephedrine, caffeine and aspirin. It is used as a cutting aid: people take it to suppress appetite, raise energy for training and burn more fat so the face and physique look leaner. It has long been popular with bodybuilders cutting fat before competitions.[1][2]

Ephedrine is a sympathomimetic stimulant that works mainly by triggering norepinephrine release. A 2021 systematic review reported about 2 kg more weight loss than placebo over 4 to 24 weeks with ephedrine, with or without caffeine; long-term effects are unknown.[1]

On looksmax.org and T Nation the stack is described as an appetite suppressant that also gives enough energy for long cardio sessions and lifting while in a calorie deficit. Forum guides pair this with warnings about heart rate and heart conditions, and its legal status varies widely by country.[2][3][8]

chain: Stimulant blunts appetite and raises energy
Easier to hold a calorie deficit and train

angle.text: Users take ECA to make cutting more tolerable: less hunger, more energy for cardio and lifting, and a modest thermogenic effect. The payoff in looks is lower body fat, which sharpens the jaw and cheeks and shows muscle separation.

infobox: Appetite suppression, energy, fat loss while cutting

paras: Ephedrine indirectly activates alpha and beta adrenergic receptors via norepinephrine release, raising blood pressure, heart rate and contractility. Animal studies show it stimulates thermogenesis in brown fat; adult humans have little brown fat, so heat production is thought to occur mainly in skeletal muscle. It also slows gastric emptying.[1] Caffeine and theophylline have a synergistic effect with ephedrine for weight loss.[1]

Caffeine on its own is described in sports-medicine literature as an ergogenic aid that can let athletes train at a greater power output or for longer.[4] Aspirin is the third component of the stack; forum posters add it for its blood-thinning effect.[3]

A 2021 systematic review found that ephedrine at the studied doses, with or without caffeine, over 4 to 24 weeks produced about 2 kg more weight loss than placebo. It also raised heart rate and HDL, lowered LDL and did not significantly change blood pressure.[1]

Common effects include insomnia, anxiety, headache, nausea, dizziness, tremor and dry mouth. Cardiovascular effects include tachycardia, arrhythmias and hypertension, and serious risks include stroke and heart attack. Psychiatric effects can include agitation and, rarely, mania or hallucinations. Combining it with MAO inhibitors can cause hypertensive crisis.[1] A review of drug-induced kidney stones lists ephedrine-containing preparations among the drugs that can cause them at high or long-term exposure.[5]

Looksmax.org guides themselves caution against use by people with heart problems, say the stack is not meant for people who do not exercise, and tell users to track resting heart rate and avoid high-intensity intervals while on it.[2][3]

In 2004 the FDA banned ephedrine alkaloids marketed for purposes other than asthma, colds, allergies or traditional Asian use; a Utah federal court ruled against the rule in 2005 and the Tenth Circuit upheld it in 2006.[1] Ephedrine is prescription-only in Australia and Germany, restricted in Canada, and is a UN Table I precursor because it can be used to make methamphetamine. It is banned by the NCAA and several professional leagues.[1] The looksmax.org ECA guide says availability depends on national law.[2]

One looksmax.org guide pitches an ephedrine and caffeine stack as an appetite killer that supports prolonged cardio, and a longer ECA guide lists the three components and when each is helpful.[2][3] Replies in the ECA thread debate which kind of exercise suits fat loss.[2]

A 17-year-old poster described running ephedrine and caffeine to "leanmaxx" and asked about adding the growth hormone secretagogue MK-677, reasoning that ephedrine would blunt the hunger MK-677 causes; a reply cautioned that a calorie deficit could work against muscle and bone growth.[6]

On T Nation, lifters describe ephedrine as part of cutting routines. One user lists an ECA stack alongside carnitine, caffeine, yohimbine and very low calories, another says he monitors resting heart rate while using the EC stack, and another says the only cutting supplements that really worked were ephedrine products sold before the US ban.[7][9][10]

Trials of ephedrine with or without caffeine for weight loss have been pooled in a 2021 systematic review, which reported about 2 kg greater loss than placebo over 4 to 24 weeks.[1] No studies were found on the ECA stack specifically for cosmetic or looksmaxxing outcomes.

timeline.event: Ephedrine introduced for medical use in the US.[1]
Tenth Circuit upholds the FDA ephedra rule.[1]

lore.intro: On looksmax.org and T Nation, ECA is presented as a cutting stack for appetite suppression and energy, with recurring warnings about heart health.[2][3][10]

claims.claim: ECA raises metabolism and suppresses appetite for fat loss.
claims.believers: A forum guide describes the stack as used for metabolism increase, appetite suppression and energy to assist weight loss.[2]
claims.experts: A 2021 systematic review found about 2 kg additional loss over placebo across 4 to 24 weeks; long-term effects are unknown.[1]

claims.claim: ECA should be combined with exercise to be worthwhile.
claims.believers: The guide states that using it without exercising is like taking a painkiller without pain.[2]
claims.experts: No published studies were found testing exercise combined with ECA specifically against ECA alone.

claims.claim: An ephedrine-caffeine stack gives energy for prolonged cardio while suppressing hunger.
claims.believers: A looksmax.org guide says the stack kills appetite and gives an energy boost that supports an hour of cardio then weights.[3]
claims.experts: Caffeine is reported to help athletes train harder or longer; ephedrine is documented to raise heart rate and blood pressure effects, including arrhythmia risk.[1][4]

claims.claim: Ephedrine can be paired with a growth-hormone secretagogue to offset its hunger.
claims.believers: A teenager on looksmax.org reasoned that ephedrine would curb the appetite increase from MK-677 while leaning out.[6]
claims.experts: No published studies were found testing this combination.

card.summary: A stimulant combination of ephedrine, caffeine and aspirin used for cutting; trials show modest short-term fat loss with cardiovascular risk.
card.note: Ephedrine alkaloid supplements are illegal to market in the US; a forum guide itself warns against use with heart problems.

quick.overview:
ECA stands for ephedrine, caffeine and aspirin. It has long been popular with bodybuilders cutting fat before competitions, and a looksmax.org guide describes it as a stack for raising metabolism, suppressing appetite and adding energy.

A 2021 systematic review found ephedrine, with or without caffeine, produced about 2 kg more weight loss than placebo over 4 to 24 weeks. Long-term effects are unknown.
quick.mechanism: Ephedrine triggers release of norepinephrine, activating adrenergic receptors; it also slows gastric emptying. Caffeine and related methylxanthines are reported to act synergistically with it.
quick.risks: Reported effects include insomnia, anxiety, tremor, rapid heart rate, arrhythmias and hypertension; stroke and heart attack are serious risks. The FDA banned ephedrine alkaloid supplements in 2004, and legal status varies by country.
